title: Bold Spicy Miso Ramen Recipe (Restaurant-Style at Home)

blocks.text: **Affiliate note:** Some links in this post may be affiliate links. If you buy through them, it helps support Date My Dish at no extra cost to you.

items: **What it is:** Spicy, creamy miso ramen with pork and a garlic-togarashi oil that turns every spoonful into a problem.
**Skill level:** Intermediate (multiple components), but each step is straightforward.
**Why it’s a date dish:** You can prep the “big flavor” pieces ahead, then assemble bowls together like a cozy little ramen shop at home.

blocks.text: The first time I made spicy miso ramen for a date, I was aiming for that *restaurant bowl at home* moment - the kind where the steam hits your face, the room smells like toasted sesame and garlic, and the conversation gets quieter because the broth is doing… a lot.

I love ramen as a date-night move because it forces you to slow down. You can’t eat it politely. You have to lean in. You have to slurp a little. And when you’re both hovering over the pot, tasting and tweaking the broth together, it stops being “dinner” and starts being a shared project.

This version is adapted from the style I learned from Mandy Lee (Lady and Pups): the **spicy miso paste** is the engine. Make it once, keep it in the fridge, and suddenly you can pull off ramen-night magic without turning your whole day into a kitchen shift.

items: **Deep, layered broth** without a 12-hour tonkotsu situation.
**Make-ahead friendly:** miso paste, eggs, and garlic oil can all live in your fridge.
**Rich but balanced:** soy milk makes it creamy without tasting like “soy milk ramen.”
**Date-night payoff:** it tastes like a ramen shop bowl, but it’s yours.

blocks.text: **Template note:** This recipe is written for **2 servings**. The spicy miso paste + garlic oil make extra (on purpose) so future ramen nights are easy.
**Spicy miso paste (makes enough for at least 8 servings)**

items: 130 g white miso paste (1/2 cup)
130 g red miso paste (1/2 cup)
80 g Sichuan douban chili paste (1/3 cup)
1 small onion (or 3/4 medium), cut into chunks
6 cloves garlic, smashed
33 g ginger (about 2 inches), cut into chunks
60 g mirin (3 tbsp)
2 tbsp vegetable oil
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp dashi granules
17 g sesame paste (2 tsp) (or tahini)
2 small shallots, finely minced
2 cloves garlic, finely minced
1/2 tsp sesame seeds
Pinch of sea salt
1/4 cup vegetable oil
2 1/2 tbsp shichimi togarashi
220 g fatty ground pork
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tbsp dried shiitake mushrooms, rinsed and finely chopped (no soaking)
1/2 tsp MSG (optional, but highly recommended)
2 cups unsalted chicken or pork stock (475 g)
1 cup unsweetened, unflavored soy milk (227 g)
3/4 cup spicy miso paste total (1/2 cup + 1/4 cup)
2 servings fresh ramen noodles
4 tbsp finely diced scallions
1 sheet nori, cut into rectangles

blocks.text: Shopping Notes (So You Don’t Overthink It)

items: **Douban (Pixian doubanjiang):** Fermented chili bean paste that makes the ramen taste legit.
**Dashi granules:** Instant umami inside the miso paste. (If you don’t eat fish, use kombu powder.)
**Soy milk:** Must be unsweetened + unflavored. Sweet soy milk will ruin the whole vibe.
**Fresh ramen noodles:** Refrigerated noodles > dried noodles > instant noodles.
**Very fine sieve:** Not mandatory, but it’s the texture cheat code.

blocks.text: 1) Make the spicy miso paste (big batch)

items: Add all miso paste ingredients to a blender and blend until smoothly pureed. Scrape down as needed.
Transfer to a pot over medium heat. Bring to a low simmer and cook, stirring, **5 minutes**.
Cool completely, then store airtight in the fridge.
Combine shallots, garlic, sesame seeds, salt, and vegetable oil in a small pot.
Cook over **low heat**, stirring, until garlic is crispy and lightly browned, **5-6 minutes**.
Turn off heat and stir in shichimi togarashi.
Let sit a few hours (or overnight) to bloom.

blocks.text: **Make-ahead win:** The miso paste, eggs, and garlic oil can all be made ahead and kept in the fridge. Date night becomes “just cook pork + noodles + assemble.”

items: Add MSG (if using): Stir it in with the broth (start with 1/2 tsp, then taste).
In a large pot, heat toasted sesame oil on high heat. Brown the ground pork with black pepper until deeply browned and it has released fat.
Add **1/4 cup** spicy miso paste and cook **1 minute** until fragrant.
Add stock and soy milk. Bring to a simmer.

Put **1/2 cup** spicy miso paste on top of a **very fine sieve**. Lower the sieve halfway into the simmering soup and use a spoon to slowly dissolve the paste into the broth. Discard solids left in the sieve.
Simmer **5 minutes**.
Cook ramen noodles according to package instructions. Drain well.
Divide noodles between two bowls and ladle broth on top.
Top each bowl with scallions, nori, and **2 tsp** garlic + togarashi oil.
Serve immediately. Slurping is encouraged.
**Before the date (Person 1):** Make/confirm miso paste + garlic oil are ready. Portion toppings (scallions, nori).
**Before the date (Person 2):** Set up bowls + chopsticks/spoons and prep toppings.
**During the date (Person 1):** Browns pork + builds broth.
**During the date (Person 2):** Cooks noodles + sets up toppings.
**Serving window (together):** Sieve in miso, taste, ladle, top, and eat while it’s screaming hot.
**It should taste salty.** If it’s “perfect” in the pot, it’ll taste bland once noodles hit.
**Don’t dump miso paste straight into the soup.** The sieve method keeps it creamy, not gritty.
**Keep soy milk below a boil.** Gentle simmer prevents weird texture.
**Make extra garlic oil.** You’ll put it on eggs, rice, roasted vegetables… everything.
Edamame with sea salt (or chili crisp if you’re feeling bold)
Quick cucumber salad (rice vinegar + sesame oil)
Gyoza (store-bought is totally valid)

blocks.text: Date Night Notes / During the Date
Ramen isn’t precious, so don’t overcomplicate it:

items: **Cold beer** (Japanese lager style is perfect)
**Dry cider** (super underrated with spicy broth)
**Chilled sake** (junmai or ginjo)
**Non-alcoholic:** Sparkling water with lime
Japanese city pop
Lo-fi beats
Anything warm and low-BPM (no chaos)
Warm the bowls if you can.
Noodles first, broth second.
Toppings on top like you’re building a little edible mood board.
Finish with that garlic-togarashi oil right at the end.
Each of you gets one bowl.
Take turns picking the next tweak: one extra spoon of miso base, a little more garlic oil, more scallions, more nori.
You’re basically seasoning each other’s bowls, and it gets surprisingly intimate.

blocks.text: Yes. Skip pork, use veggie stock, and use kombu powder instead of dashi granules.
**How long does the spicy miso paste last?**
In an airtight container in the fridge, it keeps well for at least a week (often longer).
Strongly recommended. It gives that ramen-shop creaminess.
It dissolves the good stuff and keeps gritty solids out so the broth stays rich but not thick and “sauce-like.”

items: **Prep:** ~45 min (less if components are prepped)
**Cook:** ~30 min
**Total:** ~1 hr 15 min
Brown pork with sesame oil + pepper.
Cook 1/4 cup miso paste 1 min.
Add shiitake, stock, soy milk; simmer.
Dissolve 1/2 cup miso paste through a fine sieve into broth; discard solids.
Simmer 5 min. Cook noodles. Assemble with scallions, nori, garlic oil.
